title: Release Safeguards: Decision Matrix, Escalation Ladder, and Automated Rollback Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Produce a single coordinated artifact (playbook + decision matrix + message templates) that empowers PM/Eng/Support/Trust to make fast, consistent decisions during pre-launch, launch, and post-launch incidents. This ticket covers both the decision criteria that gate an abort vs continue vs partial rollback and the concrete, tested steps to execute a rollback (automated where possible) with pre-approved internal and customer-facing messages.

Scope:
- A decision matrix that maps observable signals (latency p50/p95, error rate, model hallucination/regression metrics, billing anomalies, infra capacity warnings) to recommended actions and escalation path.
- Escalation ladder with primary/secondary owners for each functional area (runtime, infra, SDK, console, customer success). Include on-call override rules and SLA for "time-to-decision" (target: 20 minutes from detection to first action for P0).
- Automated rollback playbook: step-by-step runbook and corresponding CI/CD/GitHub actions snippets to revert to previous model variant or configuration, with a safe-fail audit trail. Include rollback verification checks and automated smoke tests.
- Standardized communications: internal incident messages (Slack runbook snippets, incident severity, hypothesis, next steps) and customer-facing templates (status page, targeted email for impacted customers, SDK changelog blurb). Provide plain and templated variants for short- and long-form comms.
- Preflight checklist for release day to reduce cognitive load: gating health checks, telemetry sanity checks, quick-bench throughput test, and explicit rollback guardrail toggles.
- Ownership and training: a 1-pager for rotation owners, and a short table-top drill plan to validate the playbook pre-launch.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decision matrix published in Confluence with a short summary in the release notes doc.
- Escalation ladder and owner roster stored in the LaunchOps on-call doc and validated with two stakeholders.
- Automated rollback scripts checked into infra repo with at least 1 PR and two approvers.
- Communications templates added to the Release Comm Templates doc and reviewed by Legal/PR/Trust.
- Runbook smoke tests pass in a staging rehearsal and the rehearsal notes are attached.

Artifacts / Links: (placeholders to be replaced during execution)
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LAUNCHOPS/pages/Release+Safeguards+Playbook
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/### (rollback automation)
- Release notes draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/rlwn-release-note-draft
- Status page template: https://status.redwood.ai/template/incident

Stakeholders: PM (Liam Patel), Eng lead - Runtime (Nora Singh), Infra SRE (Diego Morales), DevRel (Maya Roberts), Trust & Safety (Jordan Kim), Legal (Priya Shah), Support lead (Ethan Brooks).

Risks / Tradeoffs:
- Automated rollbacks reduce MTTR but can cause flapping if signal noise isn't well-understood. Decision matrix must include hysteresis/time windows.
- Aggressive rollback policies may obscure root cause; include postmortem requirements and delayed analysis windows.

Next steps (owner):
1) Draft decision matrix (Liam) by 2026-03-10.
2) Runbook automation spike (Nora/Diego) and PR by 2026-03-15.
3) Communications templates review with Legal/PR (Priya/Maya) by 2026-03-12.
4) Table-top rehearsal scheduled for 2026-03-18; rehearsal notes to be attached to this ticket.

Note: This artifact will be referenced by multiple launches (hosted API features, Dedicated capacity rollouts, Private upgrade campaigns). Design for cross-product reuse and parametric values (e.g., model name, region).
